_notes: Report functions for the OriginBI assessment platform. Import after originbi-functions.bundle.json — this bundle replaces find_candidate, list_candidates and my_report with corrected versions and adds the rest.

Report readiness is derived from the stored report rows, not from assessment_sessions.is_report_ready. That column is false on every row in the database, so anything reading it reports every report as missing.

Reports live in three places. The main report (levels 1 and 2) is one row per assessment session in assessment_reports, carrying disc_scores, agile_scores, the report number and the download URL. Level 3 (IAT) is a row per attempt in iat_reports, with a bias_map array and a narrative in report_text, ready when status = DONE. Level 4 (Metaphor) is a row per attempt in metaphor_reports, with the report body in markdown. assessment_reports.level3_scores and level4_scores are empty on every row and are not read by anything here.
An assessment level's id is NOT its level number: level 3 (IAT) is id 5 and level 4 (Metaphor) is id 3. Every level function resolves the id through assessment_levels rather than assuming.

Every query is dedup-safe: the database has exactly two physical rows per id for sessions, attempts, reports, levels and score bands, with no primary key. DISTINCT ON, COUNT(DISTINCT id) and LATERAL … LIMIT 1 make each function correct whether or not that is fixed.
A candidate may retake a level. Per-candidate functions return the most recent attempt, not every attempt.
Levels 1 (DISC) and 2 (ACI) carry a numeric score; levels 3 and 4 are pattern-based and report no mark.
ADMIN is exempt from corporate_account_id and holds "*" for allowed functions, so it picks these up on import. CORPORATE roles need the new names added to their allowed functions list.

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate.

functions.name: candidate_report_status
functions.description: Whether one candidate's reports actually exist, checked against the stored report records rather than a status flag. Returns, per assessment session: the report number, whether the main report is generated and downloadable, when it was generated, the behavioural trait code and style it produced, and separately whether the level 3 IAT report and the level 4 Metaphor report exist. Takes a registration id from find_candidate.
whenToUse: is <candidate>'s report ready
can I see <candidate>'s report
has the report been generated for this candidate
does this candidate have an IAT or Metaphor report
whenNotToUse: Not for producing a download link — that is generate_candidate_report.
Not for the scores themselves — use candidate_behavioural_profile, candidate_agile_index, candidate_iat_report or candidate_metaphor_report.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.id)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       s.id AS session_id,
       s.status AS session_status,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.session_id IS NOT NULL) AS main_report_ready,
       (ar.report_url IS NOT NULL) AS main_report_downloadable,
       ar.generated_at AS main_report_generated_at,
       pt.code AS trait_code,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       (iat.attempt_id IS NOT NULL) AS iat_report_ready,
       iat.generated_at AS iat_report_generated_at,
       (mr.attempt_id IS NOT NULL) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       mr.generated_at AS metaphor_report_generated_at,
       CASE
         WHEN ar.session_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Report is ready'
         WHEN s.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN 'Assessment finished, report not generated yet'
         ELSE 'No report — the assessment is ' || lower(coalesce(s.status, 'not started'))
       END AS readiness
  FROM registrations r
  JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_session_id AS session_id, x.report_number, x.report_url,
              x.generated_at, x.dominant_trait_id
         FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_attempt_id AS attempt_id, x.generated_at
         FROM iat_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id AND x.status = 'DONE'
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) iat ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_attempt_id AS attempt_id, x.generated_at
         FROM metaphor_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) mr ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = ar.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND r.id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY s.id DESC

functions.name: report_readiness_summary
functions.description: One row of headline counts about reports: how many candidates are registered, how many finished the assessment, how many have a main report generated, how many of those are downloadable, how many have a level 3 IAT report, how many have a level 4 Metaphor report, and how many finished but still have no report. Counted from the stored report records, so it reflects what actually exists.
whenToUse: how many reports are ready
how many registered and how many completed the assessment
how many candidates are waiting on a report
report generation status overall
whenNotToUse: Not for a per-candidate answer — that is candidate_report_status.
Not for a per-program split — that is program_report_breakdown.
Not for a per-level split — that is level_report_coverage.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH reg AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id) r.id AS registration_id, s.id AS session_id, s.status
    FROM registrations r
    LEFT JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, s.created_at DESC NULLS LAST, s.id DESC
)
SELECT count(*) AS registered_candidates,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE reg.status = 'COMPLETED') AS completed_assessment,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM assessment_reports ar WHERE ar.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id)) AS main_report_ready,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM assessment_reports ar
          WHERE ar.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id AND ar.report_url IS NOT NULL)) AS main_report_downloadable,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM iat_reports i
          WHERE i.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id AND i.status = 'DONE')) AS iat_report_ready,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM metaphor_reports mr WHERE mr.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id)) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE reg.status = 'COMPLETED' AND NOT EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM assessment_reports ar WHERE ar.assessment_session_id = reg.session_id)) AS completed_but_no_report
  FROM reg

program.description: Optional program name to narrow to, full or partial — for example "College Students".

functions.name: candidates_with_reports
functions.description: Every candidate who has a generated report, newest first, as a table: name, registration id, user id, program, report number, whether it is downloadable, their behavioural and agile totals, their trait code and style, and whether the level 3 IAT and level 4 Metaphor reports also exist. Optionally narrowed to one program.
whenToUse: show me the candidates who have reports
list the reports that are ready
give me report details for the ones who completed
which candidates can I download a report for
whenNotToUse: Not for one named candidate — use find_candidate then candidate_report_status.
Not for candidates without a report — that is list_candidates.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
         r.id AS registration_id, r.full_name AS candidate, r.user_id,
         coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program, s.id AS session_id,
         ar.report_number, ar.generated_at, ar.dominant_trait_id,
         (ar.report_url IS NOT NULL) AS downloadable,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'total')::numeric AS behavioural_total,
         (ar.agile_scores->>'total')::numeric AS agile_total
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
    LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND (cast({{param:program}} AS text) IS NULL OR p.name ILIKE '%' || {{param:program}} || '%')
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, ar.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, ar.id DESC
)
SELECT l.registration_id, l.candidate, l.user_id, l.program, l.report_number,
       l.downloadable, l.behavioural_total, l.agile_total,
       pt.code AS trait_code, pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM iat_reports i
                WHERE i.assessment_session_id = l.session_id AND i.status = 'DONE') AS iat_report_ready,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM metaphor_reports mr
                WHERE mr.assessment_session_id = l.session_id) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       l.generated_at
  FROM latest l
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = l.dominant_trait_id
 ORDER BY l.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, l.candidate

trait_code.description: Optional two-letter behavioural trait code to narrow to, for example "DI", "CD" or "CS".

program.description: Optional program name to narrow to, full or partial — for example "College Students".

functions.name: behavioural_scores_all
functions.description: A score table for every candidate who has completed level 1, the behavioural (DISC) assessment: name, registration id, user id, program, report number, the Dominance / Influence / Steadiness / Compliance breakdown, the total out of the level maximum, the trait code and blended style, the sincerity reading, and when it was completed. Highest total first. Can be narrowed to one trait code or one program. Candidates whose report has not been generated still appear, with a total but no D/I/S/C breakdown.
whenToUse: give me all the scores of students who completed level 1
export the behavioural exam scores
DISC scores for everyone
list level 1 results as a table
whenNotToUse: Not for level 2 — that is agile_scores_all.
Not for one candidate — that is candidate_behavioural_profile.
Not for a count per trait code — that is trait_code_distribution.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH lvl AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) id, max_score FROM assessment_levels WHERE level_number = 1 ORDER BY id
), att AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.registration_id)
         a.id AS attempt_id, a.registration_id, a.assessment_session_id,
         a.total_score, a.max_score_snapshot, a.sincerity_index, a.sincerity_class,
         a.dominant_trait_id, a.completed_at, lvl.max_score AS level_max
    FROM assessment_attempts a
    JOIN lvl ON lvl.id = a.assessment_level_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND a.status = 'COMPLETED'
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY a.registration_id, a.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC
)
SELECT att.registration_id, r.full_name AS candidate, r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.disc->>'D')::numeric AS dominance,
       (ar.disc->>'I')::numeric AS influence,
       (ar.disc->>'S')::numeric AS steadiness,
       (ar.disc->>'C')::numeric AS compliance,
       att.total_score AS total,
       coalesce(nullif(att.max_score_snapshot, 0), att.level_max) AS out_of,
       pt.code AS trait_code,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       att.sincerity_index AS sincerity,
       att.sincerity_class,
       att.completed_at,
       (ar.report_number IS NOT NULL) AS report_ready
  FROM att
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = att.registration_id
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.report_number, x.disc_scores AS disc
         FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = att.assessment_session_id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT s2.program_id FROM assessment_sessions s2
        WHERE s2.id = att.assessment_session_id ORDER BY s2.id LIMIT 1) sp ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(sp.program_id, r.program_id)
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = att.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE (cast({{param:trait_code}} AS text) IS NULL OR upper(pt.code) = upper({{param:trait_code}}))
   AND (cast({{param:program}} AS text) IS NULL OR p.name ILIKE '%' || {{param:program}} || '%')
 ORDER BY att.total_score DESC NULLS LAST, r.full_name

program.description: Optional program name to narrow to, full or partial — for example "College Students".

functions.name: agile_scores_all
functions.description: A score table for every candidate who has completed level 2, the Agile Compatibility Index: name, registration id, user id, program, report number, the Commitment / Focus / Openness / Respect / Courage breakdown, the total out of the level maximum, the compatibility band that total falls in, the sincerity class, and when it was completed. Highest total first. Can be narrowed to one program.
whenToUse: give me all the level 2 scores
ACI scores for everyone who completed it
agile compatibility results as a table
whenNotToUse: Not for level 1 — that is behavioural_scores_all.
Not for one candidate — that is candidate_agile_index.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH lvl AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) id, max_score FROM assessment_levels WHERE level_number = 2 ORDER BY id
), att AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.registration_id)
         a.id AS attempt_id, a.registration_id, a.assessment_session_id,
         a.total_score, a.max_score_snapshot, a.sincerity_class, a.completed_at,
         lvl.max_score AS level_max
    FROM assessment_attempts a
    JOIN lvl ON lvl.id = a.assessment_level_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND a.status = 'COMPLETED'
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY a.registration_id, a.completed_at DESC NULLS LAST, a.id DESC
)
SELECT att.registration_id, r.full_name AS candidate, r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.agile->>'Commitment')::numeric AS commitment,
       (ar.agile->>'Focus')::numeric AS focus,
       (ar.agile->>'Openness')::numeric AS openness,
       (ar.agile->>'Respect')::numeric AS respect,
       (ar.agile->>'Courage')::numeric AS courage,
       att.total_score AS total,
       coalesce(nullif(att.max_score_snapshot, 0), att.level_max) AS out_of,
       coalesce(b.level_name, 'outside the published band range') AS band,
       b.compatibility_tag AS band_summary,
       att.sincerity_class,
       att.completed_at,
       (ar.report_number IS NOT NULL) AS report_ready
  FROM att
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = att.registration_id
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.report_number, x.agile_scores AS agile
         FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = att.assessment_session_id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT s2.program_id FROM assessment_sessions s2
        WHERE s2.id = att.assessment_session_id ORDER BY s2.id LIMIT 1) sp ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(sp.program_id, r.program_id)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.level_name, x.compatibility_tag
         FROM aci_score_bands x
        WHERE x.is_active AND x.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
          AND att.total_score BETWEEN x.min_score AND x.max_score
        ORDER BY x.display_order, x.id
        LIMIT 1) b ON TRUE
 WHERE (cast({{param:program}} AS text) IS NULL OR p.name ILIKE '%' || {{param:program}} || '%')
 ORDER BY att.total_score DESC NULLS LAST, r.full_name

functions.name: trait_code_distribution
functions.description: How many candidates fall into each behavioural trait code — the two-letter DISC blend such as DI, CD, CS — with the style name that code means and each code's share of all reported candidates. Largest group first. Answers "how many are in the DI trait".
whenToUse: how many candidates are in the DI trait
breakdown by trait code
which personality styles are most common
distribution of DISC blends
whenNotToUse: Not for the names of the candidates in a code — that is candidates_by_trait_code.
Not for one candidate's style — that is candidate_behavioural_profile.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id) r.id AS registration_id, ar.dominant_trait_id
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
   WHERE ar.dominant_trait_id IS NOT NULL
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, ar.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, ar.id DESC
)
SELECT pt.code AS trait_code,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       count(*) AS candidates,
       round(100.0 * count(*) / nullif(sum(count(*)) OVER (), 0), 1) AS percent_of_reported
  FROM latest l
  JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = l.dominant_trait_id
 GROUP BY pt.code, pt.blended_style_name
 ORDER BY candidates DESC, trait_code

trait_code.description: The behavioural trait code, one or two letters — for example "DI", "CD", "CS" or "C".

functions.name: candidates_by_trait_code
functions.description: The candidates whose behavioural result is one particular trait code — the two-letter DISC blend such as DI, CD or CS — as a table: name, registration id, user id, program, report number, the style that code means, the D / I / S / C breakdown and the total. Highest total first. Answers "list the DI trait code students".
whenToUse: list the students with the DI trait code
who are the Charismatic Leaders
show me everyone in the CD trait
whenNotToUse: Not for the counts per code — that is trait_code_distribution.
Not for every code at once — that is behavioural_scores_all.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
         r.id AS registration_id, r.full_name AS candidate, r.user_id,
         coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program, ar.report_number,
         ar.dominant_trait_id,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'D')::numeric AS dominance,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'I')::numeric AS influence,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'S')::numeric AS steadiness,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'C')::numeric AS compliance,
         (ar.disc_scores->>'total')::numeric AS total,
         ar.generated_at
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
    LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
   WHERE ar.dominant_trait_id IS NOT NULL
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, ar.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, ar.id DESC
)
SELECT l.registration_id, l.candidate, l.user_id, l.program, l.report_number,
       pt.code AS trait_code, pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       l.dominance, l.influence, l.steadiness, l.compliance, l.total, l.generated_at
  FROM latest l
  JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = l.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE upper(pt.code) = upper({{param:trait_code}})
 ORDER BY l.total DESC NULLS LAST, l.candidate

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate.

functions.name: candidate_iat_report
functions.description: One candidate's level 3 IAT report as it is stored: one row per bias area with the pattern strength found, the hesitation gap in milliseconds and the error rate, plus the written narrative of the report. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Level 3 produces no numeric mark, so none is reported.
whenToUse: show me the IAT report for <candidate>
what did the level 3 report say
read the bias report for this candidate
whenNotToUse: Not for the raw per-module timing data — that is candidate_iat_patterns.
Not for level 4 — that is candidate_metaphor_report.
Not for whether it exists at all — that is candidate_report_status.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (bias.ord)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       i.generated_at,
       bias.value->>'name' AS bias_area,
       bias.value->>'pattern' AS pattern_strength,
       round((bias.value->>'speedGapMs')::numeric) AS hesitation_ms,
       round((bias.value->>'errorRate')::numeric, 1) AS error_percent,
       i.report_text AS narrative
  FROM iat_reports i
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = i.registration_id
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(i.bias_map, '[]'::jsonb)) WITH ORDINALITY AS bias(value, ord)
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND i.status = 'DONE'
   AND i.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY bias.ord, i.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, i.id DESC

registration_id.description: The candidate's registration id, as returned by find_candidate.

functions.name: candidate_metaphor_report
functions.description: One candidate's level 4 Metaphor report as it is stored: the written report and when it was generated. Takes a registration id from find_candidate. Level 4 produces no numeric mark, so none is reported.
whenToUse: show me the metaphor report for <candidate>
what did the level 4 report say
whenNotToUse: Not for level 3 — that is candidate_iat_report.
Not for whether it exists at all — that is candidate_report_status.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (mr.assessment_attempt_id)
       r.full_name AS candidate,
       mr.generated_at,
       mr.markdown AS report
  FROM metaphor_reports mr
  JOIN registrations r ON r.id = mr.registration_id
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND mr.registration_id = {{param:registration_id}}
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY mr.assessment_attempt_id DESC, mr.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, mr.id DESC

functions.name: level_report_coverage
functions.description: For each assessment level in order — level 1 Behavioural, level 2 ACI, level 3 IAT, level 4 Metaphor — how many attempts exist, how many are completed, how many reports have been generated, and which kind of report that level produces. Levels 3 and 4 keep their reports separately from the main report, and each is counted where it is actually stored.
whenToUse: how many reports exist per level
which levels are missing reports
level 3 and level 4 report coverage
whenNotToUse: Not for where candidates are stuck — that is level_completion_funnel.
Not for a single overall total — that is report_readiness_summary.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH att AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (a.id)
         a.id, a.assessment_level_id, a.status
    FROM assessment_attempts a
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = a.registration_id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY a.id
), lvl AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (id) id, level_number, name, pattern_type, sort_order
    FROM assessment_levels ORDER BY id
), generated AS (
  SELECT 1 AS level_number, count(DISTINCT ar.assessment_session_id) AS n
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
   WHERE ar.disc_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.disc_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   UNION ALL
  SELECT 2, count(DISTINCT ar.assessment_session_id)
    FROM assessment_reports ar
    JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.id = ar.assessment_session_id
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = s.registration_id
   WHERE ar.agile_scores IS NOT NULL AND ar.agile_scores <> '{}'::jsonb
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   UNION ALL
  SELECT 3, count(DISTINCT i.id)
    FROM iat_reports i
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = i.registration_id
   WHERE i.status = 'DONE'
     AND r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   UNION ALL
  SELECT 4, count(DISTINCT mr.id)
    FROM metaphor_reports mr
    JOIN registrations r ON r.id = mr.registration_id
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
)
SELECT lvl.level_number,
       lvl.name AS level,
       lvl.pattern_type AS measures,
       count(DISTINCT att.id) AS attempts,
       count(DISTINCT att.id) FILTER (WHERE att.status = 'COMPLETED') AS completed,
       coalesce(max(generated.n), 0) AS reports_generated,
       CASE lvl.level_number
         WHEN 3 THEN 'IAT narrative report (iat_reports)'
         WHEN 4 THEN 'Metaphor narrative report (metaphor_reports)'
         WHEN 5 THEN 'no report defined for this level'
         ELSE 'Main assessment report (assessment_reports)'
       END AS report_kind
  FROM lvl
  LEFT JOIN att ON att.assessment_level_id = lvl.id
  LEFT JOIN generated ON generated.level_number = lvl.level_number
 GROUP BY lvl.level_number, lvl.name, lvl.pattern_type, lvl.sort_order
 ORDER BY lvl.sort_order

functions.name: program_report_breakdown
functions.description: Registered, completed and report-ready counts for each program — School Students, College Students, Employee, CXO and so on — largest program first. Shows where reports are outstanding.
whenToUse: report readiness by program
how many college students have reports
split completions by program
whenNotToUse: Not for a per-level split — that is level_report_coverage.
Not for a single overall total — that is report_readiness_summary.
functions.sqlTemplate:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
         r.id AS registration_id,
         coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
         s.id AS session_id, s.status
    FROM registrations r
    LEFT JOIN assessment_sessions s ON s.registration_id = r.id
    LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
   WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
     AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
   ORDER BY r.id, s.created_at DESC NULLS LAST, s.id DESC
)
SELECT latest.program,
       count(*) AS registered,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE latest.status = 'COMPLETED') AS completed,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM assessment_reports ar
          WHERE ar.assessment_session_id = latest.session_id)) AS report_ready
  FROM latest
 GROUP BY latest.program
 ORDER BY registered DESC, latest.program

functions.name: my_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: whether their own reports actually exist, checked against the stored report records. Returns the report number, whether the main report is generated and downloadable, when it was generated, their trait code and style, and separately whether the level 3 IAT report and the level 4 Metaphor report exist. Returns only the caller's own records.
whenToUse: is my report ready
what is my report number
can I download my report
do I have an IAT or metaphor report
whenNotToUse: Not for whether the assessment itself is finished — use my_assessment_status.
Not for producing a download link — that is generate_my_report.
Only ever returns the caller's own data.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (s.id)
       s.id AS session_id,
       s.status AS session_status,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       ar.report_number,
       (ar.session_id IS NOT NULL) AS main_report_ready,
       (ar.report_url IS NOT NULL) AS main_report_downloadable,
       ar.generated_at AS main_report_generated_at,
       pt.code AS trait_code,
       pt.blended_style_name AS style,
       (iat.attempt_id IS NOT NULL) AS iat_report_ready,
       (mr.attempt_id IS NOT NULL) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       CASE
         WHEN ar.session_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Report is ready'
         WHEN s.status = 'COMPLETED' THEN 'Assessment finished, report not generated yet'
         ELSE 'No report — the assessment is ' || lower(coalesce(s.status, 'not started'))
       END AS readiness
  FROM assessment_sessions s
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = s.program_id
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_session_id AS session_id, x.report_number, x.report_url,
              x.generated_at, x.dominant_trait_id
         FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id
        ORDER BY x.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, x.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_attempt_id AS attempt_id
         FROM iat_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id AND x.status = 'DONE'
        ORDER BY x.id DESC LIMIT 1) iat ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT x.assessment_attempt_id AS attempt_id
         FROM metaphor_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id
        ORDER BY x.id DESC LIMIT 1) mr ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN personality_traits pt ON pt.id = ar.dominant_trait_id
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY s.id DESC

functions.name: my_iat_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their own level 3 IAT report as it is stored — one row per bias area with the pattern strength, the hesitation gap in milliseconds and the error rate, plus the written narrative. Level 3 produces no numeric mark, so none is reported.
whenToUse: show me my IAT report
what did my level 3 report say
read my bias report
whenNotToUse: Not for the raw per-module timing data — that is my_iat_patterns.
Not for level 4 — that is my_metaphor_report.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (bias.ord)
       i.generated_at,
       bias.value->>'name' AS bias_area,
       bias.value->>'pattern' AS pattern_strength,
       round((bias.value->>'speedGapMs')::numeric) AS hesitation_ms,
       round((bias.value->>'errorRate')::numeric, 1) AS error_percent,
       i.report_text AS narrative
  FROM iat_reports i
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(i.bias_map, '[]'::jsonb)) WITH ORDINALITY AS bias(value, ord)
 WHERE i.status = 'DONE'
   AND {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY bias.ord, i.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, i.id DESC

functions.name: my_metaphor_report
functions.description: For the signed-in student: their own level 4 Metaphor report as it is stored — the written report and when it was generated. Level 4 produces no numeric mark, so none is reported.
whenToUse: show me my metaphor report
what did my level 4 report say
whenNotToUse: Not for level 3 — that is my_iat_report.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (mr.assessment_attempt_id)
       mr.generated_at,
       mr.markdown AS report
  FROM metaphor_reports mr
 WHERE {{scope:user_id}}
 ORDER BY mr.assessment_attempt_id DESC, mr.generated_at DESC NULLS LAST, mr.id DESC

name.description: The candidate's name, full or partial.

registration_id.description: The registration id, if it is already known.

functions.name: find_candidate
functions.description: Find one candidate (a registered person) within your company by their name, and return the identifiers other functions need: their registration id, their user id, the program they are on, the status of their latest assessment session, and whether their main, IAT and Metaphor reports have actually been generated. When several people match the name it returns them as choices rather than picking one.
whenToUse: find the candidate called <name>
look up <name>
which registration is <name>
whenNotToUse: Not for a list of everyone — that is list_candidates.
Not for a platform user by email — that is find_user.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
       r.id AS id,
       r.full_name AS label,
       coalesce(p.name, 'no program') || ' · ' || coalesce(s.status, 'no session yet')
         || ' · ' || CASE WHEN ar.n > 0 THEN 'report ready' ELSE 'no report' END AS detail,
       CASE
         WHEN r.id = {{param:registration_id}} THEN 100
         WHEN lower(r.full_name) = lower({{param:name}}) THEN 100
         ELSE 70
       END AS match_score,
       r.full_name,
       r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       r.status AS registration_status,
       coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       (ar.n > 0) AS report_ready,
       (iat.n > 0) AS iat_report_ready,
       (mr.n > 0) AS metaphor_report_ready
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT s2.id, s2.status, s2.program_id
         FROM assessment_sessions s2
        WHERE s2.registration_id = r.id
        ORDER BY s2.created_at DESC NULLS LAST, s2.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) s ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM iat_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id AND x.status = 'DONE') iat ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM metaphor_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id) mr ON TRUE
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND (
        r.full_name ILIKE '%' || {{param:name}} || '%'
     OR r.id = {{param:registration_id}}
   )
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY r.id

session_status.description: Optional session status to narrow to.

functions.name: list_candidates
functions.description: List the candidates registered under your company, each with their registration id, user id, program, the status of their latest assessment session, and whether their main, IAT and Metaphor reports have actually been generated. Optionally narrowed to one session status.
whenToUse: list our candidates
who is registered
show me everyone who has not started
whenNotToUse: Not for one named person — that is find_candidate.
Not for only those with reports — that is candidates_with_reports.
functions.sqlTemplate:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (r.id)
       r.id,
       r.full_name,
       r.user_id,
       coalesce(p.name, 'unassigned') AS program,
       coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') AS session_status,
       (ar.n > 0) AS report_ready,
       (iat.n > 0) AS iat_report_ready,
       (mr.n > 0) AS metaphor_report_ready,
       r.created_at
  FROM registrations r
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT s2.id, s2.status, s2.program_id
         FROM assessment_sessions s2
        WHERE s2.registration_id = r.id
        ORDER BY s2.created_at DESC NULLS LAST, s2.id DESC
        LIMIT 1) s ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN programs p ON p.id = coalesce(s.program_id, r.program_id)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM assessment_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id) ar ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM iat_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id AND x.status = 'DONE') iat ON TRUE
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
       SELECT count(DISTINCT x.id) AS n FROM metaphor_reports x
        WHERE x.assessment_session_id = s.id) mr ON TRUE
 WHERE r.is_deleted IS NOT TRUE
   AND (cast({{param:session_status}} AS text) IS NULL
        OR coalesce(s.status, 'NO_SESSION') = {{param:session_status}})
   AND {{scope:corporate_account_id}}
 ORDER BY r.id
